title: I Took the Airbnb House-Rules Email to the Host's Own Review

parts.text: I arrived at 4:20 p.m. to a lockbox that stuck and a list of house rules that had grown since booking. No shoes. No cooking smells. Quiet hours at 8. Checkout photos of every drawer. I was thirty-seven on a work trip with a rolling bag and a yogurt I was not allowed to smell. The listing had said relaxed home. A camera in the living room had a sticker: for safety. The message thread showed the host adding rules after my payment. I cooked pasta anyway because the kitchen was in the photos. At 8:07 the host texted that the camera heard a pan. I photographed the listing, the new rules, and the camera sticker. Then the host said they would keep the deposit for "unauthorized cooking."
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They are keeping the deposit for pasta in a kitchen they advertised.

social.video_title: The house rules multiplied after I paid — Part 1/2
social.description: Lockbox, yogurt, and a camera that listens to pans. The listing said relaxed. Would you have eaten cereal for three days?

parts.text: I sent the thread to Airbnb support with the original listing text: full kitchen. They restored the deposit and flagged the post-booking rules. I left a review that quoted the listing and the 8:07 pan text. The host replied that guests should be grateful. I was grateful for a stove. I washed the pan. I took checkout photos because I am not trying to lose a deposit twice. The yogurt stayed quiet. The camera watched me leave at noon like a person who had used a kitchen as a kitchen.

social.video_title: Support restored the deposit the pan supposedly spent — Part 2/2
social.description: Full kitchen in the listing, pasta in real life, review in writing. Was a camera a lease addendum?
